---
title: "DNAnexus basics"
---

Before starting JupyterLab, there is one important idea to understand:

> **Your DNAnexus project keeps your files. JupyterLab provides the temporary computer you use to work with them.**

Once this distinction is clear, the rest of the workflow becomes much easier to understand.

## Your DNAnexus project

A **project** is the area in DNAnexus that you have been given access to.

The project contains the files you need for your work. Depending on why you are using DNAnexus, these might include:

- your workspace;
- shared training materials;
- notebooks;
- approved research data; and
- saved analysis outputs.

Files stored in the project are **persistent**. This means they remain there when you finish your work and terminate JupyterLab.

::: {.callout-note title="Project = persistent"}
Think of your DNAnexus project as the place where your files are kept.

You can leave DNAnexus, come back later, and the files stored in the project will still be there.
:::

## Your workspace

On the previous page, we introduced the term **your workspace**.

For this tutorial, this simply means the folder in the project where you keep your own work.

Your supplied training notebook will be located there:

```text
your workspace/
└── getting-started.ipynb
```

Remember that **workspace** is just a term we use in this tutorial to keep the instructions simple. It is an ordinary folder in the DNAnexus project.

## JupyterLab

**JupyterLab** is where you run R and perform your analysis.

When you start JupyterLab, DNAnexus gives you a temporary computer with:

- processing power;
- memory; and
- software such as R.

You do not need to install R on your own computer to complete the tutorial.

You use JupyterLab to:

- open your notebook;
- run R code;
- read data from your DNAnexus project;
- produce tables and figures; and
- inspect your results.

When you are finished, you **terminate** the JupyterLab environment.

::: {.callout-tip title="A useful way to think about it"}
Imagine that your **DNAnexus project is a filing cabinet** and **JupyterLab is a computer next to it**.

Your files remain in the filing cabinet when you switch the computer off.

The next time you start JupyterLab, you get a new temporary computer that can access the same project files.
:::

## What is saved and what is temporary?

This distinction is important:

| Saved in your DNAnexus project | Temporary in JupyterLab |
|---|---|
| Your `[DX]` notebook | The running R session |
| Files in your workspace | Objects currently held in R memory |
| Shared onboarding files | The active computing environment |
| Approved project data | Temporary files that you have not saved back to the project |

For example, later in this tutorial you will read a synthetic data file into R:

```r
dat <- read.csv(
  "/mnt/project/mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/data/example_data.csv"
)
```

There are two different things here:

1. `example_data.csv` is a **file stored persistently in the DNAnexus project**.
2. `dat` is an **R object held temporarily in the current R session**.

If you terminate JupyterLab, the original `example_data.csv` file remains in the project.

The R object `dat` does not remain in memory. The next time you start JupyterLab, you can simply run the code again to recreate it.

::: {.callout-note title="This is good practice in R"}
Your notebook contains the code needed to recreate your analysis.

Rather than relying on objects remaining in memory, you should be able to rerun your notebook to recreate the objects you need.
:::

## Your `[DX]` notebook

For this tutorial, you will use a **DNAnexus Notebook**.

You can recognize one because its name is shown with **`[DX]`** when it is open in JupyterLab:

```text
[DX] getting-started.ipynb
```

A `[DX]` notebook is stored persistently in your DNAnexus project.

When you save it, the notebook can preserve:

- your R code;
- text and notes;
- tables;
- model summaries; and
- figures displayed in the notebook.

We have designed the tutorial so that the `[DX]` notebook is the main place where you keep a record of your analysis.

::: {.callout-warning title="Look for `[DX]`"}
For this tutorial, always open the supplied `getting-started.ipynb` notebook from **your workspace**.

When it opens, check that **`[DX]` appears in the notebook tab**.

This confirms that you are working with the persistent DNAnexus Notebook supplied for the tutorial.
:::

## How R sees your project files

When R is running inside JupyterLab, files stored in your DNAnexus project are available under:

```text
/mnt/project/
```

You do not need to understand the technical details of this path.

For this tutorial, just remember:

> **`/mnt/project/` means "files in my current DNAnexus project".**

For example:

```text
/mnt/project/mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/data/example_data.csv
```

means:

```text
my DNAnexus project
└── mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/
    └── data/
        └── example_data.csv
```

Later, the required paths will already be provided in your notebook. You will not need to type them from memory.

## Putting everything together

The relationship between the main pieces is:

```text
DNAnexus project
(persistent)
│
├── your workspace/
│   └── getting-started.ipynb  ← persistent [DX] notebook
│
└── mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/
    └── data/
        └── example_data.csv   ← persistent training data

                 │
                 │ accessed from
                 ▼

             JupyterLab
             (temporary)
                 │
                 ▼
                 R
                 │
                 ├── dat
                 ├── models
                 └── other objects
                     held temporarily in memory
```

The key idea is:

<div class="mcps-workflow-summary">

**Project files persist → JupyterLab is temporary → `[DX]` notebooks save your analysis**

</div>

## Computing resources and cost

Starting JupyterLab uses computing resources provided through DNAnexus.

Before starting an environment, DNAnexus will show you:

- the **Instance Type**, which determines the computing resources available;
- the **Duration** of the environment; and
- an **Estimated Price**.

You will choose these settings on the next page.

::: {.callout-caution title="Terminate JupyterLab when you finish"}
JupyterLab uses computing resources while the environment is running.

When you finish your work, **terminate the JupyterLab environment**.

Simply closing the browser tab does not necessarily stop the computing environment.
:::

## Ready to start JupyterLab?

You now know the four concepts you need:

**Project**
The area in DNAnexus where your files are stored.

**Workspace**
The folder where you keep your own work during this tutorial.

**JupyterLab**
The temporary computer you use to run R.

**`[DX]` notebook**
The persistent notebook where you keep your analysis.

Next, you will start your first JupyterLab environment.
